chunks: 'Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Let no one intercede regarding a hadd once it has reached the Imam, for then he possesses authority over it. But intercede in matters that have not reached the Imam when you see remorse. And intercede before the Imam in other than the hadd, with the approval of the one for whom intercession is sought. And do not intercede concerning the right of a Muslim man or anyone else except with his permission.”

key_terms.النَّدَمَ: remorse indicating repentance over the offense
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the legitimate authority before whom judicial matters are brought
key_terms.الْمَشْفُوعِ لَهُ: the person on whose behalf intercession is made
key_terms.حَدٍّ: a prescribed legal punishment fixed by the Sacred Law
key_terms.حَقِّ: an established right or claim belonging to a person
key_terms.يَشْفَعَنَّ: to intercede or plead on behalf of someone

ai.seo_question: When is intercession permitted or forbidden in hadd cases and other rights according to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets boundaries for shafa'ah in legal and personal matters. It forbids intercession in a hadd case once it has formally reached the Imam, permits intercession before that point when repentance is evident, and requires the consent of the concerned person when interceding in matters involving personal rights.
